steps.description:

allContributions.title: Get Started with Accessibility Features
allContributions.description: Learn the tools and shortcuts that make VSLight accessible. Note that some actions are not actionable from within the context of the walkthrough.

steps.title: Use the accessibility help dialog to learn about features
steps.description:
The accessibility help dialog provides information about what to expect from a feature and the commands/keybindings to operate them.
 With focus in an editor, terminal, or comment, the relevant dialog can be opened with the Open Accessibility Help command.
[Open Accessibility Help](command:editor.action.accessibilityHelp)

steps.title: Screen reader users can inspect content line by line, character by character in the accessible view.
steps.description:
The accessible view is available for the terminal, hovers, notifications, comments, and inline completions.
 With focus in any of those features, it can be opened with the Open Accessible View command.
[Open Accessible View](command:editor.action.accessibleView)

steps.title: Control the verbosity of aria labels
steps.description:
Screen reader verbosity settings exist for features around the workbench so that once a user is familiar with a feature, they can avoid hearing hints about how to operate it. For example, features for which an accessibility help dialog exists will indicate how to open the dialog until the verbosity setting for that feature has been disabled.
 These and other accessibility settings can be configured by running the Open Accessibility Settings command.
[Open Accessibility Settings](command:workbench.action.openAccessibilitySettings)

steps.title: Unlock productivity with the Command Palette
steps.description:
Run commands without reaching for your mouse to accomplish any task in VSLight.
[Open Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands)

steps.title: Customize your keyboard shortcuts
steps.description:
Once you have discovered your favorite commands, create custom keyboard shortcuts for instant access.
[Keyboard Shortcuts](command:toSide:workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings)

steps.title: Fine tune which accessibility signals you want to receive via audio or a braille device
steps.description:
Accessibility sounds and announcements are played around the workbench for different events.
 These can be discovered and configured using the List Signal Sounds and List Signal Announcements commands.
[List Signal Sounds](command:signals.sounds.help)
[List Signal Announcements](command:accessibility.announcement.help)

steps.title: Access the hover in the editor to get more information on a variable or symbol
steps.description:
While focus is in the editor on a variable or symbol, a hover can be focused with the Show or Open Hover command.
[Show or Focus Hover](command:editor.action.showHover)

steps.title: Navigate to symbols in a file
steps.description:
The Go to Symbol command is useful for navigating between important landmarks in a document.
[Go to Symbol](command:workbench.action.gotoSymbol)

steps.title: Use code folding to collapse blocks of code and focus on the code you're interested in.
steps.description:
Fold or unfold a code section with the Toggle Fold command.
[Toggle Fold](command:editor.toggleFold)
 Fold or unfold recursively with the Toggle Fold Recursively Command
[Toggle Fold Recursively](command:editor.toggleFoldRecursively)

steps.title: Use Intellisense to improve coding efficiency
steps.description:
Intellisense suggestions can be opened with the Trigger Intellisense command.
[Trigger Intellisense](command:editor.action.triggerSuggest)
 Inline intellisense suggestions can be triggered with Trigger Inline Suggestion
[Trigger Inline Suggestion](command:editor.action.inlineSuggest.trigger)
 Useful settings include editor.inlineCompletionsAccessibilityVerbose and editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion.

steps.title: Configure accessibility settings
steps.description:
Accessibility settings can be configured by running the Open Accessibility Settings command.
[Open Accessibility Settings](command:workbench.action.openAccessibilitySettings)

steps.title: Safely browse and edit code
steps.description:
[Workspace Trust](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/workspace-trust) lets you decide whether your project folders should **allow or restrict** automatic code execution __(required for extensions and tasks)__.
Opening a file/folder will prompt to grant trust. You can always [enable trust](command:toSide:workbench.trust.manage) later.

media.altText: Workspace Trust editor in Restricted mode and a primary button for switching to Trusted mode.

limitations: Main/shared-process ChannelServer maps are outside the renderer CDP context.
Statusbar capture reads existing model entry IDs and alignment only; names, tooltips, commands, DOM and getters are not evaluated.
Process and logs prove the observed interval only; they do not prove future background inactivity.
Empty MenuId symbols are reported separately from registered menu items.
No walkthrough service/collection means no positive evidence that ordinary walkthroughs are retained.
